generated workloads run in a namespace of their own by default (blong-services), so the first pass
that got past generation reported five read failures — first
PersistentVolumeClaim/blong-services/mysql-data — and converged nothing. The tree now carries one
Role and RoleBinding pair per namespace a pass touches: the suite's, each backing service's, and the
namespace the deployment asked for. The lesson is the same one the node rule taught: rights a pass
needs are not visible in unit tests, they are visible in one run against a cluster, so an end-to-end
run belongs at the end of a change like this rather than in a follow-up.

Fixed. One operator Role and RoleBinding pair per namespace a pass touches. Verified on the
dev-cluster: the pair is created in blong-services by the suite's own tree, and the pass then reads
and applies there.

### F-459 — Two fill DaemonSets went on running from the previous approach

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The fill is one Job per node now — a template in the tree, instantiated per node by the overlay — so
nothing the realm emits is a DaemonSet. Two cache DaemonSets nevertheless ran for twenty hours, one
in the suite's namespace and one in the install's, each with its two pods, because the generation
that created them was the last one written before the switch. What made the residue cost more than a
delete was the prose: ten places still named a prefetch or cache DaemonSet — two generator comments,
a resources note beside it, the operator entry's artifact comment, three files in the harness lib,
and two suite config comments — so a report of the end-to-end run could read the cluster's leftovers
as the tree's own objects and describe a fill DaemonSet that no file contains. The user spotted it
and asked for the drop. The lesson is that a change of resource kind needs two sweeps: the cluster,
for objects no tree names any more, and the prose, which is what a reader trusts when the cluster
disagrees.

Dropped by hand on the dev-cluster: both cache DaemonSets deleted and their pods gone, with no
DaemonSet left in the cluster. The eleven prose sites that still named one now name the fill Job,
verified by prettier and by the lint runs of realm/blong-kustomize, test/blong-int-kustomize and
suite/blong-suite plus the realm's 85 tests.

### F-460 — A caller that relied on the layout default

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The operator's child generation named a layout only when the artifact shipped a base, so the realm's
new base default reached the other path: an artifact packaged before the split would have had the
child write a design half, and the pass would have applied placeholder values — PLACEHOLDER labels,
a hostPath of the mount, a claim named after the suite. Nothing tested that child: a grep for a spec
of kustomizeSuiteGenerate finds only its implementation, so the question the user asked was the only
thing between the change and a broken pass on an old artifact. Both paths now name their layout, and
every launch of a generation in the repository does — the operator's child, the runbook's two suite
halves, and its operator install tree, which a grep for the k8s argument confirms.

Fixed: the operator's child names the layout on both paths — local when the artifact ships a base,
flat when it does not — and the two documents that read a bare generation as split now say it writes
the design half. Verified: realm specs 85/85, realm and markdown lints clean, and a grep for every
launch of a generation shows each naming its layout.

### F-480 — A switched-off service was read from a namespace nobody named

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

A pass over a switched-off service read `service/mysql` with no namespace at all, so the Kubernetes
client used `default`, the operator's service account was refused there, and the whole pass ended
`Failed`: five objects it planned to create never were, `status.deployments` kept the service, and
the runbook's wait for the switch to be observed timed out after five minutes. The declaration stops
naming the services namespace exactly when the last service is switched off — the field travels with
a generated service — so the one case that must find a retired object is the case that has nowhere
to look. Read the CR's status and the operator's log before believing a tree assertion: the tree
said the switch was honoured and the cluster said the pass never ran.

The switch now reaches the operator's composition and the shared namespace: kustomizeSuiteGenerate
leaves a switched-off service's folder behind instead of copying it, materializeGeneratedTree
composes only the folders the overlay's backing child names, and listingScopes adds the services
namespace for generated credentials so the label's exception can take one back. The
SERVICE_OFF=mysql run is green end to end: the plan drops mysql, the alias and the credentials copy
go from the tenant's namespace, the generated Secret goes from the shared one, and the workload, its
claim and its Service stay there as obsolete (D-461). The earlier closure of T-321 asserted that
removal from a wait while the pass could not reach the object — the assertion was right and the code
was not.

### F-481 — The declaration never named the namespace the operator retires from

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

A pass over a suite whose declaration carried no `servicesNamespace` read `service/mysql` and
`persistentvolumeclaim/mysql-data` with no namespace at all, so the Kubernetes client used
`default`, the operator's service account was refused there, and the pass ended `Failed` with the
five objects it planned to create never applied — mysql kept its place in `status.deployments` and
the runbook's wait timed out after five minutes. The generator writes the field only when the
deployment overrides the default, and its own objects default to `blong-services`, so the omission
reads like tidiness: the operator resolves the namespace of an object it managed before from the
declaration rather than from the plan's default, and a field nobody wrote is a read in the wrong
namespace. The cluster kept a stale declaration from an older generator that carried the field,
which is why the defect appeared only once the runbook began applying the declaration it generates
(F-478).

Fixed in the generator: the declaration now carries the effective services namespace (the
deployment's own override, or the blong-services the workloads default to), so the operator resolves
its own objects there instead of falling back to its client's namespace, where its account is
refused. Pinned by a test in testServiceCatalog and verified on the cluster: the pass reports Ready
with no failures and the plan names mysql and its four siblings.

### F-486 — The mounted fill module started as a no-op

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The program guard compared import.meta.url with `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])`, and that can never
match for a copy mounted from a ConfigMap: the kubelet publishes a mount as a symlink to a versioned
directory, so the module url names the versioned path while argv names the path the Job typed. The
fill Jobs reported Completed seconds after starting and published nothing, and every reader stayed
Pending on a hostPath of type Directory that nobody created — which reads as a slow rollout and
looked like the process ignoring SIGTERM. Not one unit test could see it, because they all call
fillFromEnvironment directly rather than starting the module as a program. The guard matches by
realpathSync now, and a test spawns the module through a symlink (T-318).

Fixed by matching the program entry with realpathSync against fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), and
testFill now spawns the module through a symlink to a versioned directory, which is the shape a
ConfigMap mount has. The realm suite is 111/111.

### F-487 — The fill unpacked a 653 MB artifact into memory

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

unpackZip read the whole archive with readFileSync and inflated each entry in one go, while the fill
Job template gives that container 512Mi — and this suite's artifact is 653 MB. The unpack was
OOMKilled part-way, leaving a half-written .staging directory on both nodes, so the identity the
deployment reads never appeared and the suite rollouts timed out with one old replica pending
termination. The reader walks the file through a descriptor now and streams each entry through
inflate into its file, and a test pins the resident memory an unpack spends, which is the one part
of this a unit test can reach (T-318).

Fixed: unpackZip walks the archive through a file descriptor and streams each entry through
createInflateRaw into its file, and a test pins the resident memory an unpack spends. The realm
suite is 111/111 and a cluster cycle filled both nodes and started the whole suite.

### F-494 — Every authenticated call dies in the codec handshake

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The 500 is not the method being called: it is the gateway codec reaching the `login` service. The
gateway error carries the cause `EAI_AGAIN` for hostname `login.default.svc.cluster.local`;
`ResolutionK8s` builds that name from the service and the namespace, and `busGateway` is the ky
caller that posts to the identity endpoints of the target. This realm replaces blong-login but
answers only `login.token.create`, so any call needing a bearer makes the codec resolve a `login`
method the local port cannot answer, the call leaves the process for the `login` service that does
not exist, and DNS fails — which is why every method 500s, invented methods included, while
`login.token.create` (auth login, no handshake) answers with its own typed error. The layer and
model wiring is fine: the loader loads `meta` and the model reaches the subject orchestrator.

The codec transport and the framework HTTP helper now raise errors that name the address, the method
and the resolver code, and the gateway logs the cause of an unhandled error, so an unreachable
dependency names itself instead of reading as a bare fetch failed. The unreachable call was the
identity discovery of the login service, now switched off.

### F-493 — Port-forward shadowed by a local operator

> _2026-10-11 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

An operator process started locally in an earlier turn held port 8098, so the port-forward of 8098
to the operator pod never bound and every request meant for the pod was answered by that local
process instead, with its own defects, its own gateway port and its own build of the UI. Hours of
evidence came from the wrong process, including a pod log that looked silent because the pod was
never asked and a page whose shell came from the local `dist`. The lesson: prove the tunnel before
trusting what answers at its far end, by asking who owns the port after starting the forward (a
`kubectl` process, not a node process) and by probing the pod for a line the local process could not
have written.

### F-499 — The realm CLI loads a database nobody asked for

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The realm CLI now dies with Unknown database and it is not caused by the framework changes in
flight: the same command fails with the committed Remote restored, so it is the working tree or the
environment around it rather than canSkipSocket. The command is enough to see it, from the realm
directory: node --conditions=development bin/kustomize.ts keys-ensure --namespace=blong-system, and
adding --server.adapter=false makes it succeed, which says the difference is the framework realm db
adapter starting inside a CLI that has no database and no reason to open one. The deny is written as
server.adapter false in the realm index default block, which is the spelling that reaches the
framework realm from a parent config, so something between the two is losing it. The delivery cycle
runs exactly this command in its machine prepare half, so the whole cycle stops there: build and
deploy never happen.

### F-504 — A realm cannot read the private signing key out of the gateway config

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The first session mint read `gateway.config().sign` and failed with
`The "key.d" property must be of type string. Received undefined`: `mle.ts` deliberately writes
the **public** half back over `gateway.sign`/`gateway.encrypt` so private material never sits in
readable configuration (D-448), so a handler scope can never reach the private half. The key has to
be the realm own configuration (`kustomize.login.session.key`), which is also how the framework own
login realm is given its key, and the deployment writes it into the same generated rc document as
the gateway pair (`kustomizeGatewayKeysEnsure.gatewayKeysConfig`).

Resolved by design: the private sign key reaches the realm as its own configuration
(`kustomize.login.session.key`), written into the same generated rc document as the gateway pair,
because `mle.ts` writes the public half back over `gateway.sign` by design (D-448). The realm suite
pins the mint and the published key set.

### F-505 — A port reads its own config slice and a gateway route folder is the subject

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

Two address mistakes, each costing a cycle. First: the session config was written under
`kustomize.deploy.session.*` while the mint lives in the login port, and a dispatch port reads
`mergedConfig.<realm>.<namespace>` — so the mint refused with `sessionUnconfigured` although the
block was in the entry all along; it had to move to `kustomize.login.session.*`. Second: a gateway
file folder is the _subject_ and the file name is the rest of the method, so
`gateway/session/oidc.getConfiguration.ts` is `session.oidc.getConfiguration` at `/rpc/session/...`,
while `gateway/kustomize/session.oidc.getConfiguration.ts` resolves to a namespace whose handler
does not exist. A _method with no handler_ registers no route at all, and an unknown path under
`/rpc/` answers 401 `missing authorization header` from the bearer hook rather than 404 — which
reads exactly like `auth: false` not working.

Resolved: the session config lives at `kustomize.login.session.*` (the port that mints reads it),
and the two public routes live at `gateway/session/oidc.getConfiguration.ts` and `oidc.getKeys.ts`,
which makes them `session.oidc.*` at `/rpc/session/...` — the shape whose method the session port
actually serves. The lesson is in the friction: a method with no handler registers no route, and an
unknown `/rpc/` path answers 401 rather than 404.

### F-500 — One cluster token, many browsers, one recorded handshake

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The session a realm answers is keyed by the identity the cluster gives the caller, and a
service-account token is the same identity for every browser that presents it. Two Playwright tests
in one file log in one after the other under that one token, the second login overwrites the first
pair, and the first page's still-open session then signs with a pair the gateway no longer holds:
the call is refused as a signature failure and the test that passed alone fails in a suite. Seen
exactly like that with the reconcile test, which failed in the file and reached its handler when run
by name. The durable fix is the one D-530 points at, letting the caller keys travel with each call;
until then the realm entry is honest about its bound, and the handshake is one per identity, not one
per session.

Fixed and verified. The login no longer hands back the cluster token: it mints a session of its own
(`sessionToken.ts` + `orchestrator/login/sessionTokenMint.ts`) signed with the gateway sign key and
carrying the caller MLE pair as `enc`/`sig`, a `ses` claim so the framework skips its session step,
the `sub` the caller logged in as, and the verified cluster identity as `clusterUser`. The realm
serves the issuer discovery document and key set as public routes, and the deployment writes the
private pair into the same generated rc document as the gateway pair. The whole cluster spec now
passes — 3 passed — where before every test in the file failed with
ERR_JWS_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILED as soon as two logins shared the service account. The
per-process registry (mleHandshake) is left in place for a caller that presents the cluster token
itself; nothing records into it for a browser any more.

### F-501 — One setting, two names: config nodes vs spec nodeSource

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The node source is `nodes` in the realm merged config (`IPlanConfig.nodes`) and `nodeSource` in a
`BlongDeployment` spec, deliberately, because the spec file the tree writer reads carries `nodes` as
the resolved names. Writing the spec name into `operator-entry.ts` type-checked, passed the
114-strong realm suite and every snapshot, and reached the cluster only as a silent no-node plan:
the reconcile refused with "the plan names no nodes". Both names with the reason now sit next to
each other in the entry, but the lesson is that a rename between the two shapes is invisible to
lint, tests and snapshots and appears only as a runtime refusal from the process that read the wrong
one.

Resolved by documenting both names where they meet: `operator-entry.ts` now names `nodes` (the realm
config, a selector or a list) and the CR field `spec.nodeSource` in adjacent comments, with the
reason — the spec file the tree writer reads carries `nodes` as the resolved names. The delivery
path proved the lesson the hard way: the wrong key type-checked, passed 114 tests and every
snapshot, and appeared only as a runtime refusal from the operator.

### F-507 — A stale visual baseline neither fails nor gets rewritten

> _2026-10-12 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

The user spotted that a committed-looking baseline
(`test-cluster/deployments.play.ts-snapshots/kustomize-deployment-browse-linux.png`) still showed an
error: an empty Deployment table and an `Error / Not Found` dialog, which is the pre-fix state from
when the read method had no route (F-497), with an mtime a day old. The comparison was running all
along — with the baseline moved aside Playwright failed and wrote the actual — and it passed because
the framework budget is `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`, a share of a 1600x900 image, while the difference
between the error page and the healthy one measured 12316 pixels (0.86 percent), just inside it.
Resolved by asking for `maxDiffPixels: 50` in the cluster config and redacting the one volatile cell
(the `Created` timestamp) through the helper own `redact` option, then regenerating the baseline
from the running operator: with the old baseline the run now fails at the same 12316 pixels, with
the new one it passes, and the whole cluster spec is 3 passed. See D-534.

### F-617 — The suite version fallback answers with the generator's own package

> _2026-10-27 · realm/blong-kustomize · resolved_

`suiteVersion(plan)` asks the _generator's_ own manifest first — `import.meta.url` of `generator.ts`
is the kustomize realm's file, which always exists — so the `plan.suite.entry` fallback after it
never runs, and its comment ("never required, so no suite repeats a value its package holds") is
wrong. With `kustomize.deploy.suite.version` removed from `realm/blong-sport/index.ts` and the
kustomize package temporarily set to 9.9.9, the generated tree carried 9.9.9: the realm's version,
not the suite's. A suite therefore keeps naming its version in its own config, and making that
automatic needs the suite's manifest to reach the plan — the registry reporting its `pkg`, or the
runbook passing `--kustomize.deploy.suite.version` from the package it was told to deploy — rather
than another fallback. The `pkg` field in the definition is the opposite case: the loader fills
`mod.pkg` from the manifest for a server suite, so declaring it repeats two values the package
already holds.

Resolved by D-646: the plan takes the suite version from the loaded package's manifest, so the
generator's fallback — which asks the kustomize realm's own package — is no longer reached for a
loaded suite.
